result.description: Code hosting and developer collaboration platform (repos, issues, PRs, Actions, orgs) with REST and GraphQL APIs.
result.auth_detail: OAuth2 via OAuth Apps (web flow, device flow) and GitHub Apps (user-to-server OAuth, installation tokens via app JWT); fine-grained and classic personal access tokens sent as bearer; GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions. Basic auth with PAT also works.
result.access_detail: Any free GitHub account can register an OAuth App or GitHub App and create PATs. No Marketplace listing, app review or paid plan needed for other users/orgs to authorize or install; org owners may restrict third-party apps, but that is an org setting, not vendor review. Some features (e.g. private-repo advanced security, enterprise endpoints) are plan-gated, but core API is free.
result.api_notes: REST API (versioned, OpenAPI described, hundreds of endpoints: repos, issues, PRs, actions, orgs, users, checks, packages, etc.) plus GraphQL v4 API and webhooks.

evidence.quote: You can create a personal access token, generate a token with a GitHub App, or use the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN in a GitHub Actions work
Both OAuth apps and GitHub Apps use OAuth 2.0.
GitHub Apps can act on behalf of a user, similar to an OAuth app, or as themselves, which is beneficial for automations that do not require user input.
GitHub chose GraphQL because it offers significantly more flexibility for our integrators.
Many REST API endpoints require authentication or return additional information if you are authenticated.
The remote GitHub MCP Server is hosted by GitHub and provides the easiest method for getting up and running.
This gives AI agents, assistants, and chatbots the ability to read repositories and code files, manage issues and PRs, analyze code, and automate workflows.
